accuracy_vs_baseline.note: scored at each run's true hazard zone (run-level, not pooled across all 7 zones)

zone_localization.note: fraction of compound test runs where the model's highest-scoring zone (of all 7) matches the zone the dual-fault was actually injected into

lead_time.note: negative = detected before/at ground-truth onset (anticipatory); positive = detected N samples (3 min each) after onset; both measured at the run's true hazard zone. NOT a headline metric: with permit/presence visibility properly time-gated (no future-leak), the GNN does not detect earlier than the baseline on this benchmark -- training data was not time-gated, so the model learned 'permit visible => compound' and correctly waits for the permit to actually appear before committing. The model's real advantages are precision/zone-localization, not lead time -- see accuracy_vs_baseline and zone_localization above.
